key_insight: Deep representation-based out-of-distribution detection identified unfamiliar DNA methylation profiles, with 1D-Subspace Analysis performing best among five tested methods.
clinical_relevance: This approach could provide a quality-control layer for methylation-based tumor classification by flagging samples outside a model’s training distribution; it does not evaluate cancer drugs.
method: Train deep neural classifiers on public sarcoma and brain tumor methylation cohorts.
Extract 200- and 500-dimensional bottleneck embeddings and compare five OOD detection methods.
Use spectral discrepancy to distinguish in-distribution from out-of-distribution samples.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included cross-validation, holdout samples, and an independent clinical dataset, where the method achieved mean AUROC 0.976 and TNR@95TPR 0.935.
watch_item: Performance on broader unseen tumor types and across laboratory platforms requires validation before routine clinical deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data
